explanation: Fish represent the largest vertebrate group, ranging from a few millimeters to 12 meters in length. Jawless Fish (Agnathans) are cylindrical (up to a meter long), have smooth, non-scaly skin, act as scavengers feeding on dead fish, and include lampreys. Fish with jaws are ectotherms (body temperature regulated by the environment), and possess gills, a bony endoskeleton, and scales (including extinct placoderms). Cartilaginous fish possess a cartilage skeleton instead of bone, 5-7 open gill slits (no gill cover), teethlike scales, and include sharks, rays, skates, and chimaeras.

questions.q: Which fish are characterized by cylindrical bodies, smooth non-scaly skin, scavenger habits, and include lampreys?

questions.q: Which characteristics are shared by all fish with jaws?
opts: Ectotherms with gills, bony endoskeleton, and scales

questions.q: What features distinguish cartilaginous fish from bony fish?
opts: A cartilage skeleton instead of bone, 5-7 gill slits with no cover, and teethlike scales
A bony skeleton, a swim bladder, and flat scales
A cylindrical body with smooth nonscaly skin and no jaws
